item.title: #3587797: Move views data cache to cache_discovery
item.description:
• Project: Drupal Core
  • Type: Normal task
  • Version: main
  • Status: Fixed
  • Changes: 4 files, +8/−19 · php +8/−19
  • Diff: 7d8143e
  • Discussion: #3587797 · 7 contributors · 40 comments
  • Followers: 10
  • AI disclosures: 0 of 7 contributors

Summary

Views builds a large in-memory data structure describing every database table exposed to Views (via hook_views_data()), and caches it both as one big entry and as many smaller per-table entries. Per-table entries were previously stored in the regular persistent cache (cache.default); they are now stored in the cache.discovery bin, which is chained with a fast, per-process backend like APCu when available. Since the set of tables is finite and rebuilt rarely, this lets repeat lookups for the same table on a page be served from local memory instead of the primary cache backend (Redis, database, etc.), reducing cache reads on pages that use Views. The single "all views data" entry stays in cache.default because it can be very large and the maintainers were concerned that pushing it into a fast in-memory bin could evict other cached data on large, multilingual sites.

Impact

Affects module maintainers.

  • Deprecation: \Drupal\views\ViewsData::cacheGet() and cacheSet() are deprecated in Drupal 11.5.0 and removed in 12.0.0, with no replacement.

Technical details

The initial commit simply swapped the constructor's #[Autowire] target for ViewsData::$cacheBackend from cache.default to cache.discovery, but this was reverted after berdir pointed out that the combined "all tables" entry can be tens of megabytes on sites with many languages or entity bundles, and forcing all of that into the chained-fast (APCu-backed) bin risked frequent APCu expunges and a performance regression rather than an improvement.

The follow-up perf commit instead adds a second injected backend, $chainedFastBackend (cache.discovery), used only for the per-table cache entries in ViewsData::get(), while getData() keeps using $cacheBackend (cache.default) for the full "all tables" entry. A new ViewsData::CACHE_TAGS constant centralizes the views_data and config:core.extension cache tags used when setting either bin. The old protected cacheGet()/cacheSet() helpers, which always prefixed the langcode and used $cacheBackend, are no longer used internally and are deprecated with @trigger_error; callers should use the injected cache backends directly, following how the rest of the class now works.

Performance test fixtures (FrontPageTest, StandardPerformanceTestTrait, Umami/Standard profile test YAMLs) were updated to reflect the shift: discovery cache-get counts go up and default cache-get counts go down by the same amount, confirming per-table lookups now hit cache.discovery.

Upgrade

Subclasses or code relying on \Drupal\views\ViewsData::cacheGet() or cacheSet() will get a deprecation notice starting in Drupal 11.5.0 and must stop using them before 12.0.0, since there is no direct replacement method. Interact with the injected $cacheBackend (cache.default, for the "all data" entry) or the new $chainedFastBackend (cache.discovery, for per-table entries) directly instead:

// Before (deprecated):
$data = $this->cacheGet($cid);
$this->cacheSet($cid, $data);

// After, for per-table entries:
$data = $this->chainedFastBackend->get($this->prepareCid($cid));
$this->chainedFastBackend->set($this->prepareCid($cid), $data, Cache::PERMANENT, static::CACHE_TAGS);

Contribution

Timeline

  • Opened: April 30, 2026
  • First commit: April 30, 2026
  • Last commit: August 27, 2026 (3 months and 3 commits later)

Key contributors

  • catch (Tag1 Consulting, Inc.)
  • alexpott (Acro Commerce)
  • berdir (MD Systems GmbH)

Collaboration

catch proposed moving the whole ViewsData cache to cache_discovery and alexpott committed it, but berdir flagged a regression risk: on large or heavily multilingual sites the combined "all tables" cache entry can be megabytes in size, and pushing that into APCu-backed chained-fast storage risks frequent expunges that hurt performance more broadly (citing real-world monitoring data from sites using an APCu-expunge sensor). alexpott reverted the commit the same day. berdir then measured actual cache entry sizes with a script run against a production-like Redis dataset, showing the "all tables" entries were an order of magnitude larger than the sum of per-table entries, and suggested moving only the per-table entries into the fast bin. catch implemented that split (two injected cache backends), and the two also floated further ideas (a hook_views_data_table()-style API, and not caching views data per-language) that were not pursued in this issue. berdir later reviewed again and preferred catch's simplified follow-up that dropped the old cacheGet/cacheSet helpers entirely in favor of calling the backends directly, calling it "much nicer."

item.title: #3472624: Ensure the UI dialog instance is valid in Drupal.dialog.resetSize
item.description:
• Project: Drupal Core
  • Type: Critical bug report
  • Version: 11.x-dev
  • Status: Fixed
  • Changes: 3 files, +66/−3 · php +35 · js +31/−3
  • Diff: d0904d4
  • Discussion: #3472624 · 15 contributors · 36 comments
  • Followers: 21
  • AI disclosures: 1 of 15 contributors

Summary

Opening a modal dialog and closing it again very quickly (within about 20 milliseconds) could throw an uncaught JavaScript error, "cannot call methods on dialog prior to initialization; attempted to call method 'option'", because a scheduled dialog resize callback ran after the dialog had already been destroyed. This could interrupt other JavaScript on the page and was also causing intermittent failures in Drupal core's own JavaScript test suite. The fix ensures a resize that is still pending when a dialog closes is cancelled instead of running against a dialog that no longer exists.

Impact

Affects module maintainers.

  • New API: Drupal.debounce() now returns a function that has a cancel() method, letting callers abort a scheduled invocation that has not run yet.

Technical details

The root cause was in misc/dialog/dialog.ajax.js: Drupal.dialog.resetSize is invoked via Drupal.debounce on window resize/scroll events, but the dialog:beforeclose handler only unbound those event listeners; it could not stop a resize call that had already been scheduled by debounce's internal setTimeout. By the time that timeout fired, the dialog's DOM element (and its jQuery UI instance) had already been removed, so calling .dialog('option', ...) on it threw.

The fix has two parts. misc/debounce.js's Drupal.debounce now returns a function that also carries a cancel() method, which clears the pending timeout so a scheduled call never runs. dialog.ajax.js stores the autoResize debounced function on the dialog element via $element.data('drupalAutoResize', autoResize) when the dialog opens, and its dialog:beforeclose handler now calls $(e.target).data('drupalAutoResize')?.cancel() before unbinding the resize/scroll handlers. As a defensive second layer, resetSize() also now bails out early if event.data?.$element?.data('ui-dialog') is falsy, i.e. the jQuery UI dialog instance is no longer present. Test coverage was added in DialogTest that opens a modal, triggers a resize, immediately closes the dialog, and asserts no JS errors are logged.

A change record (#3619513, referenced in comments) documents the new debounce().cancel() API for other core and contrib code that debounces callbacks tied to DOM elements that may be removed.</technical> <parameter name="collaboration">The bug lingered for a long time with several reporters (grimreaper, goz, joseph.olstad, albeorte) confirming related but not-quite-matching symptoms with CKEditor and other dialog-triggering modules, and earlier MR attempts did not fully resolve it for them. The issue was escalated to Critical by longwave after noting in #16720832 that the flakiness had "got much worse" following #3515403 (the Selenium/Chrome upgrade), since it was now causing multiple JS test failures in core. Longwave then diagnosed the actual mechanism, that dialog:beforeclose unbinds handlers but cannot stop an already-scheduled debounced call, and implemented the debounce.cancel() fix with new test coverage, noting the diagnosis and fix were assisted by Claude Code. godotislate stress-tested the fix by repeating a previously flaky test 500 times without failure to confirm the intermittent failures were resolved before it was marked RTBC again.</collaboration> <parameter name="upgrade">

item.title: #3619447: Avoid rebuilding the router twice when uninstalling a profile in the installer
item.description:
• Project: Drupal Core
  • Type: Normal task
  • Version: 11.x-dev
  • Status: Fixed
  • Changes: 1 file, +6/−5 · php +6/−5
  • Diff: 8cb43d9
  • Discussion: #3619447 · 3 contributors · 9 comments
  • Followers: 3
  • AI disclosures: 0 of 3 contributors

Summary

When a Drupal installation profile is configured to be uninstalled right after installation (as Drupal CMS's installer profile does), the installer was rebuilding the routing table twice in a row: once implicitly because uninstalling the profile module always rebuilds the router, and once explicitly at the end of install_finished(). Each rebuild took around 450ms in testing, so this doubled work was adding noticeable time to the last step of installation. The fix skips the redundant explicit rebuild in that case, so installs that uninstall their profile finish faster with no change in the end result.

Impact

No upgrade or configuration changes required.

Technical details

In install_finished(), the explicit \Drupal::service('router.builder')->rebuild() call is now only made in the branch where the profile is kept ($install_state['profile_info']['keep_profile'] is true). When the profile is instead uninstalled via \Drupal::service('module_installer')->uninstall([$profile]), that call's own module uninstall process already triggers a router rebuild, so the subsequent explicit rebuild was pure duplicate work. The comment explaining why the rebuild is needed at all (the installer never fires KernelEvents::TERMINATE, which normally triggers this rebuild via an HTTP kernel) was moved alongside the remaining call site.

item.title: #1189464: Add an 'instant' queue runner
item.description:
• Project: Drupal Core
  • Type: Normal feature request
  • Version: 11.x-dev
  • Status: Fixed
  • Changes: 6 files, +233/−40 · php +223/−40 · yml +10
  • Diff: 9a96116
  • Discussion: #1189464 · 13 contributors · 75 comments
  • Followers: 54
  • AI disclosures: 0 of 13 contributors

Summary

Drupal has had two ways to run long tasks: the Queue API (normally only drained by cron) and the blocking Batch API. This issue adds a middle ground: an "instant queue runner" service that modules can hand a queue name to during a request, and a handful of items (5 by default) from that queue get processed right after the response has been sent to the browser, without blocking the user. This is opt-in per queue, not automatic for all queues, so existing sites see no behavior change until a module or contrib project starts using it. The maintainers point to use cases like closing a timing-attack window on the password reset form (#3316209), instant search indexing, and image style pre-warming as the reasons this landed now.

Impact

Affects module maintainers and site owners.

  • Config change: New instant_queue.config container parameter with a maximumItems key (default 5) caps how many items per queue the instant runner processes per request.
  • New API: New Drupal\Core\Queue\InstantQueueRunnerInterface service lets modules register a queue name so a few of its items get processed right after the response is sent, instead of waiting for cron.

Technical details

The new Drupal\Core\Queue\InstantQueueRunner service implements InstantQueueRunnerInterface (a single registerQueue(string $queue_name): void method) and DestructableInterface, and is tagged needs_destruction so its destruct() runs during kernel.terminate. During a request, code that adds an item to a queue also calls registerQueue(); the runner just counts how many times each queue name was registered. In destruct(), for each registered queue it claims and processes up to min(maximumItems, $count) items (default maximumItems is 5, configurable via the instant_queue.config container parameter), stopping early if a worker throws SuspendQueueException.

To avoid duplicating the claim/process/exception-handling logic, the per-item processing loop previously inlined in Cron::processQueue() was extracted into a new Drupal\Core\Queue\QueueProcessTrait::processItem(), which handles DelayedRequeueException, RequeueException, SuspendQueueException, and generic \Throwable logging via Error::logException(). Both Cron and InstantQueueRunner now use this trait, so the exception semantics for queue workers are identical whether items run via cron or via the instant runner.

Nothing in core actually calls registerQueue() yet: no core queue was converted as part of this change, and integration with automated_cron was deliberately dropped from scope (comment #16451928) in favor of a simpler, opt-in-per-caller design without added concurrency protection. A follow-up (#3617085) proposes using it for field purging.

Upgrade

Modules that want a queue item processed shortly after the request that created it, instead of waiting for cron, can inject the new interface and register the queue name after adding the item:

public function __construct(
  protected QueueFactory $queueFactory,
  protected \Drupal\Core\Queue\InstantQueueRunnerInterface $instantQueueRunner,
) {}

public function someMethod() {
  $this->queueFactory->get('my_queue')->createItem($data);
  $this->instantQueueRunner->registerQueue('my_queue');
}

Sites can change how many items get processed per queue per request by overriding the instant_queue.config container parameter (default maximumItems: 5) in a services.yml.

Contribution

Timeline

  • Opened: June 15, 2011
  • Committed: August 27, 2026 (15 years and 2 commits later)

Key contributors

  • catch (Tag1 Consulting, Inc.)
  • berdir (MD Systems GmbH)
  • tsphethean
  • sukr_s
  • smustgrave (Mobomo)
  • heddn (MTech, LLC)
  • nicxvan (nLightened Development LLC)
  • godotislate

Collaboration

This issue sat open for over a decade with several proposed designs (1px-gif poor-man's-cron style pings, async HTTP requests, ReactPHP/Fibers). catch repeatedly steered it back toward using the post-response terminate event rather than async HTTP, noting in comment #15616106 and #16452204 that async self-requests don't work reliably on all hosting environments, and that terminate-based processing became solid after #3295790 fixed destructable services actually blocking. sukr_s built the first working merge request implementing this with automated_cron integration and a concurrency semaphore, but after review catch decided in comment #16451928 that this carried more complexity than needed (automatic integration with all queues via automated_cron, and the semaphore) and opened a second, simplified MR that made registration opt-in per caller and extracted the shared per-item processing logic into QueueProcessTrait. After commit, berdir raised an unresolved concern (comment #16749447) that capping by item count rather than by time could still exhaust php-fpm worker processes on hosts with very low process counts, since a slow queue item keeps a process busy in the background even though the response was already sent.

item.title: #3580152: Deprecate theme-settings.php files
item.description:
• Project: Drupal Core
  • Type: Normal task
  • Version: 11.x-dev
  • Status: Fixed
  • Changes: 5 files, +148/−121 · php +148/−121
  • Diff: 0757aeb
  • Discussion: #3580152 · 6 contributors · 35 comments
  • Followers: 8
  • AI disclosures: 0 of 6 contributors

Summary

Themes have historically been able to put certain hook implementations, most commonly hook_form_system_theme_settings_alter(), in a special theme-settings.php file that Drupal auto-loads. Now that hooks can be implemented as attribute-based classes and can live in their own files, this special-cased file is deprecated and will stop being supported in Drupal 12. Core's own Olivero theme has been converted as an example: its theme settings form alter now lives in an OOP hook class instead of olivero/theme-settings.php. Any theme (core, contrib, or custom) that still ships a theme-settings.php file will now trigger a deprecation notice, and should convert its code before Drupal 12.0.0.

Impact

Affects module maintainers.

  • Deprecation: Using a theme-settings.php file in a theme is deprecated in Drupal 11.5.0 and will be removed in Drupal 12.0.0; convert hook implementations to attribute-based OOP hook classes (or move them to the theme's .theme file if legacy support below 11.3 is needed).

Technical details

The deprecation is enforced in ThemeHookCollectorPass::collectThemeHookImplementations(): when a discovered file is identified as a theme's theme-settings.php ($isThemeSettings), an E_USER_DEPRECATED notice is triggered pointing to the change record at drupal.org/node/3587273, in addition to the file still being loaded and its procedural hooks still working through Drupal 12.

Olivero's olivero/theme-settings.php was removed and its olivero_form_system_theme_settings_alter() logic moved verbatim into a new Drupal\olivero\Hook\OliveroThemeSettingsHooks class, implementing hook_form_FORM_ID_alter() via the #[Hook('form_system_theme_settings_alter')] attribute and using StringTranslationTrait::t() instead of the procedural t().

The test_theme_settings test theme's theme-settings.php was deliberately left in place to preserve legacy procedural-hook test coverage; the affected functional tests (FileFieldWidgetTest/related theme settings form tests) were updated with #[IgnoreDeprecations] and expectUserDeprecationMessage() calls, with a comment noting that file should be converted once support for the deprecated behavior is fully removed. The related issue #3581218 similarly deprecates the .theme file extension itself.

Upgrade

Convert any hook implementations in a theme's theme-settings.php to an attribute-based hook class, following the Olivero example:

namespace Drupal\mytheme\Hook;

use Drupal\Core\Form\FormStateInterface;
use Drupal\Core\Hook\Attribute\Hook;

class MythemeThemeSettingsHooks {

  #[Hook('form_system_theme_settings_alter')]
  public function formSystemThemeSettingsAlter(array &$form, FormStateInterface $form_state): void {
    // Moved logic from theme-settings.php here.
  }

}

Then delete theme-settings.php. If the theme must simultaneously support versions of Drupal older than 11.3 alongside Drupal 12, move the hook implementation to the theme's .theme file instead, but note that .theme files are themselves deprecated (see #3581218) and will need converting again later.

Contribution

Timeline

  • Opened: March 19, 2026
  • Committed: August 27, 2026 (5 months and 2 commits later)

Key contributors

  • nicxvan (nLightened Development LLC)
  • debdeep.mukhopadhyay (Innoraft)
  • smustgrave (Mobomo)
  • mstrelan (PreviousNext)
  • catch (Tag1 Consulting, Inc.)

Collaboration

Early attempts at converting Olivero's file (by debdeep.mukhopadhyay and rajivgandhi chinnakrishnan) ran into review pushback from nicxvan, who found the submitted MR and patch deleted over 100 lines unexpectedly and asked "why did you change the hook implementation so much?" and "can you both please provide information on how you did the conversion." nicxvan ultimately closed that MR and redid the conversion directly. Later, mstrelan raised a substantive concern that recommending theme maintainers move code to a .theme file was odd given .theme files are themselves being deprecated (#3581218); nicxvan clarified in response that moving to .theme is only a fallback recommendation for themes needing simultaneous support below Drupal 11.3, and updated the change record for clarity.

item.title: #3555115: Add a UploadedFilesExtractor and remove duplicate code
item.description:
• Project: Drupal Core
  • Type: Normal task
  • Version: 11.x-dev
  • Status: Fixed
  • Changes: 5 files, +61/−72 · php +59/−72 · yml +2
  • Diff: 7817455
  • Discussion: #3555115 · 9 contributors · 35 comments
  • Followers: 11
  • AI disclosures: 0 of 9 contributors

Summary

Drupal core had the same logic for pulling uploaded files out of the current HTTP request duplicated in several places: the procedural file_save_upload() and file_managed_file_save_upload() functions, and ConfigImportForm::validateForm(). This issue consolidates that logic into a single reusable service. There is no behavior change for site owners or end users; file uploads via forms, the managed file element, and configuration import all continue to work exactly as before.

Impact

Affects module maintainers.

  • New API: New Drupal\Core\File\UploadedFilesExtractor::extractUploadedFiles() service method for retrieving uploaded files for a given form element name from the current request.

Technical details

A new Drupal\Core\File\UploadedFilesExtractor service (autowired in core.services.yml) exposes extractUploadedFiles(string $name): UploadedFile[], which reads $this->requestStack->getCurrentRequest()->files->get('files', []), looks up the given form element name, and normalizes the result to always return an array (wrapping single uploads). file_save_upload() and file_managed_file_save_upload() in file.module now call this service via \Drupal::service(UploadedFilesExtractor::class) instead of inlining the request lookup and array-normalization logic. ConfigImportForm was also converted to constructor-based dependency injection using AutowireTrait and PHP attributes, and its validateForm() now calls the injected UploadedFilesExtractor and uses reset($uploaded_files) to get the single tarball upload.

The fourth duplicate identified in the issue, Drupal\Core\Render\Element\File::valueCallback(), was deliberately left untouched: its handling casts the uploaded file object to an array, which the issue authors considered "different and strange" and out of scope for this cleanup (an early attempt to convert it was reverted during review).

Contribution

Timeline

  • Opened: October 29, 2025
  • Committed: August 26, 2026 (10 months and 2 commits later)

Key contributors

  • kim.pepper (PreviousNext)
  • smustgrave (Mobomo)
  • nicxvan (nLightened Development LLC)
  • berdir (MD Systems GmbH)
  • mohit_aghera (PreviousNext)
  • quietone (PreviousNext)
  • godotislate
  • catch (Tag1 Consulting, Inc.)

Collaboration

The issue sat for a while before nicxvan picked it up, rebased it, and argued the extraction logic should be a proper service rather than a method taking the request as a parameter, since every caller needed the current request anyway. While testing, nicxvan hit a Serialization of 'UploadedFile' is not allowed exception coming from Drupal\Core\Batch\BatchStorage, but confirmed through further testing that this failure pre-existed the patch and was unrelated to the refactor. berdir reviewed the resulting MR and pointed out the issue summary needed updating since the File::valueCallback() case was no longer being converted, prompting mohit_aghera to write a change record (later refined after quietone flagged a leftover reference to $form_field_name in it).</collaboration> <parameter name="upgrade">Code that previously duplicated the uploaded-file lookup can now use the injected service instead:

use Drupal\Core\File\UploadedFilesExtractor;

// Via dependency injection:
public function __construct(
  protected UploadedFilesExtractor $uploadedFilesExtractor,
) {}

// ...
$uploaded_files = $this->uploadedFilesExtractor->extractUploadedFiles('import_tarball');
if (!empty($uploaded_files)) {
  $file_upload = reset($uploaded_files);
}

Or via the service container:

$uploaded_files = \Drupal::service(UploadedFilesExtractor::class)->extractUploadedFiles($form_field_name);

item.title: #3618358: Deprecate remaining underscore functions in locale
item.description:
• Project: Drupal Core
  • Type: Normal task
  • Version: 11.x-dev
  • Status: Fixed
  • Changes: 9 files, +417/−277 · php +417/−277
  • Diff: ee8c2fa
  • Discussion: #3618358 · 4 contributors · 16 comments
  • Followers: 6
  • AI disclosures: 0 of 4 contributors

Summary

This is a cleanup of Drupal core's locale (interface translation) subsystem: the last remaining procedural, underscore-prefixed helper functions used to rebuild and invalidate JavaScript translation files have been deprecated. Their logic has been moved into the existing LocaleJs service class. Site owners are not affected functionally; this only matters to developers or contributed modules that call these low-level functions directly.

Impact

Affects module maintainers.

  • Deprecation: Six locale.module underscore functions (_locale_refresh_translations(), _locale_refresh_configuration(), _locale_strip_quotes(), _locale_parse_js_file(), _locale_invalidate_js(), _locale_rebuild_js()) are deprecated in Drupal 11.5 for removal in Drupal 13.0; most have replacements on the Drupal\locale\LocaleJs service.

Technical details

The six functions' bodies were moved onto Drupal\locale\LocaleJs as methods (refreshTranslations(), parseJsFile(), invalidate(), rebuild()), or dropped with no replacement (_locale_refresh_configuration(), _locale_strip_quotes(), both folded inline or made a private stripQuotes() helper). The old functions now just emit an E_USER_DEPRECATED trigger_error and delegate to \Drupal::service(LocaleJs::class). parseJsFile() and rebuild() remain public (rather than the protected originally proposed in the issue summary) but are marked @internal, because tests call them directly; only stripQuotes() became protected.

To support this, LocaleJs's constructor gained several new dependencies (StringStorageInterface, LocaleLanguages, LanguageManagerInterface, PluralFormulaInterface, FileSystemInterface, a lazy logger closure, and EventDispatcherInterface), and LocaleFileManager's constructor gained an optional ?LocaleJs $localeJs parameter; omitting it triggers its own deprecation notice and falls back to \Drupal::service(LocaleJs::class). Call sites in locale.module, TranslateEditForm, and locale's hook implementations were updated to call the service directly instead of the deprecated functions. As a drive-by fix, the @see link on the already-deprecated locale_string_is_safe() was corrected to point to the right change record.

Upgrade

Replace direct calls to the deprecated functions with the LocaleJs service:

// Before:
_locale_refresh_translations($langcodes, $lids);
_locale_invalidate_js($langcode);
_locale_parse_js_file($filepath);
_locale_rebuild_js($langcode);

// After:
\Drupal::service(\Drupal\locale\LocaleJs::class)->refreshTranslations($langcodes, $lids);
\Drupal::service(\Drupal\locale\LocaleJs::class)->invalidate($langcode);
\Drupal::service(\Drupal\locale\LocaleJs::class)->parseJsFile($filepath);
\Drupal::service(\Drupal\locale\LocaleJs::class)->rebuild($langcode);

_locale_refresh_configuration() and _locale_strip_quotes() have no replacement; inline the equivalent logic if still needed. Custom services extending or instantiating LocaleFileManager directly should pass a LocaleJs instance as the new constructor argument to avoid the deprecation notice.

item.title: #3539178: Extract _user_mail_notify() into a user NotificationHandler
item.description:
• Project: Drupal Core
  • Type: Normal task
  • Version: 11.x-dev
  • Status: Fixed
  • Changes: 13 files, +685/−185 · php +684/−185 · yml +1
  • Diff: c222ded
  • Discussion: #3539178 · 13 contributors · 114 comments
  • Followers: 18
  • AI disclosures: 0 of 13 contributors

Summary

Drupal's user module used to send all of its notification emails (registration, password reset, account activated/blocked/canceled, cancellation confirmation) through a single internal function, _user_mail_notify(). Despite its underscore prefix marking it as internal, this function turned out to be called directly by dozens of contributed modules. Its logic has now been extracted into a new NotificationHandler service, one method per notification type (sendPasswordReset(), sendStatusActivated(), sendRegisterAdminCreated(), etc.). _user_mail_notify() itself still works exactly as before but is now formally deprecated, with a longer-than-usual grace period: it will be removed in Drupal 13.0.0 rather than sooner, specifically to give contrib maintainers time to update. This groundwork lets an experimental future mail system swap in a different notification implementation without touching user module internals directly.

Impact

Affects module maintainers.

  • Deprecation: _user_mail_notify() is deprecated in drupal:11.5.0 for removal in drupal:13.0.0; its logic moved into the new (currently @internal) Drupal\user\NotificationHandler service.

Technical details

The new Drupal\user\NotificationHandler class lives in core/modules/user/src/NotificationHandler.php, is registered as an unaliased, autowired service (Drupal\user\NotificationHandler: ~), and is marked @internal with no interface: the maintainers deliberately did not want to commit to a public contract yet (see the long back-and-forth over whether to make it public, settled by an @internal-for-now compromise). It injects logger.channel.user and plugin.manager.mail as lazy \Closure values via #[AutowireServiceClosure] rather than eager services. All the old $op-dispatch logic from _user_mail_notify() is preserved in a protected sendToUser(string $op, UserInterface $account): ?bool method; the public methods (sendCancelConfirm(), sendPasswordReset(), sendStatusActivated(), sendStatusBlocked(), sendStatusCanceled(), sendRegisterAdminCreated(), sendRegisterNoApprovalRequired(), sendRegisterPendingApproval()) each wrap it and cast the result to bool, discarding the old NULL vs FALSE distinction that _user_mail_notify() still exposes for BC.

Call sites across user module were updated to use the new service: UserAuthenticationController, UserCancelForm, UserPasswordForm, RegisterForm, Drupal\rest\Plugin\rest\resource\UserRegistrationResource, and User::postSave(). Summary

Drupal core's entity reference field API now uses PHP 8.4 property hooks to expose the entity and target_id properties on entity reference field items and item lists, instead of relying on PHP's __get()/__set() magic methods. This removes a fragile workaround that was needed to avoid a PHP bug where suspending a Fiber inside __get() could incorrectly trigger PHP's recursion guard, and it also fixes isset() checks on these properties inside a running Fiber, since PHP routes isset() through a property hook's get accessor but not through __isset().

Impact

Affects module maintainers.

  • API change: entity and target_id on EntityReferenceItem and EntityReferenceFieldItemList are now declared as typed properties with PHP 8.4 property hooks instead of being handled by __get()/__set() magic methods; unset() on either property now throws Error: Cannot unset hooked property instead of silently clearing the value.

Technical details

Previously, EntityReferenceItemBase::__get() special-cased the entity property: when called while a Fiber was already running, it wrapped the call to parent::__get() in a new Fiber and manually pumped resume()/usleep() until it terminated, to dodge a PHP fiber/recursion-guard bug (php/php-src#14983). That override is now removed entirely; EntityReferenceItemBase is back to an empty class body.

Instead, EntityReferenceItem declares entity and target_id as typed properties (?EntityInterface $entity and string|int|null $target_id) using property hooks: the get hook delegates to the existing __get() logic and the set hook calls $this->set(). EntityReferenceFieldItemList gets the same two hooked properties, with get proxying to $this->first()?->__get(...) and set appending a field item if needed before calling $item->set(). item.title: #3534109: Permanently maintain a sandbox directory in package_manager
item.description:
• Project: Drupal Core
  • Type: Major task
  • Version: 11.x-dev
  • Status: Fixed
  • Changes: 6 files, +629/−69 · php +623/−69 · yml +6
  • Diff: f31a5d8

  • Followers: 9
  • AI disclosures: 0 of 6 contributors

Summary

Package Manager (used by Automatic Updates, Project Browser, and other update tooling) used to copy the entire codebase into a fresh, randomly-named sandbox directory for every composer operation, then delete it afterwards. On hosts with limits on file operations (some shared/managed hosting providers), this churn of tens of thousands of file creates and deletes per operation could trip usage caps and lock accounts. Now Package Manager keeps a single sandbox directory around permanently and reuses it for every operation, so rsync only needs to copy files that actually changed instead of recreating the whole codebase each time. Stale sandboxes are cleaned up automatically during cron after a configurable number of days (14 by default), and the directory is still deleted immediately if a site turns off include_unknown_files_in_project_root, since leftover excluded files would otherwise never get removed.

Impact

Affects module maintainers and site owners.

  • Config change: New optional $settings['package_manager_max_sandbox_age'] (default 14 days) controls how long the now-persistent Package Manager sandbox directory is kept before cron deletes it.
  • API change: SandboxManagerBase::destroy() no longer deletes the sandbox directory (it stays on disk for reuse) and no longer queues cleanup via the package_manager_cleanup queue; getSandboxDirectory() now returns a fixed path (sandbox_directory, not a random per-stage name) and no longer throws \LogicException when called before the stage is created or claimed.

Technical details

The sandbox directory's name changed from a per-stage random token to a fixed sandbox_directory constant (SandboxManagerBase::COMPOSER_SANDBOX_DIRECTORY) under the site's staging root, so the same physical directory is reused across create/destroy cycles. SandboxManagerBase::destroy() was simplified to just release the lock and mark the stage available; it no longer deletes the directory or enqueues it to the package_manager_cleanup queue (the Cleaner queue worker itself is untouched, pending a possible follow-up to remove it). sandboxDirectoryExists() now means "the stage is actively claimed and its directory exists on disk," which is a different question from "does the directory physically exist," since a long-lived sandbox persists after destroy().

Because Composer Stager's stock StagingDirDoesNotExistInterface precondition expects an empty target, a new Drupal\package_manager\StagingDirDoesNotExist decorator was added that always reports the precondition as fulfilled, letting the sandbox be reused even though it already exists. Two new pieces of infrastructure manage the directory's lifecycle: EventSubscriber\LongLivedSandboxSubscriber records the timestamp of the last PostCreateEvent in state (package_manager.last_create_event), and deletes the sandbox immediately when package_manager.settings:include_unknown_files_in_project_root transitions from TRUE/unset to FALSE. Hook\CronHook (a #[Hook('cron')] implementation) compares that timestamp against Settings::get('package_manager_max_sandbox_age', 14) (in days) and deletes the sandbox if it's stale and not currently locked. getSandboxDirectory() and getStagingRoot() were also relaxed to work without an active lock (needed since cron and the config subscriber must locate the directory outside of a claimed stage), but getStagingRoot() only caches its result in the shared tempstore when a lock is actually held, to avoid polluting shared state from incidental lookups.

Upgrade

Code that calls SandboxManagerBase::getSandboxDirectory() before creating or claiming a stage will no longer get a \LogicException; it now returns the deterministic sandbox path directly. Code that relied on destroy() deleting the sandbox directory (or on the package_manager_cleanup queue running shortly after) must not assume the directory is gone until cron has run and the configured package_manager_max_sandbox_age has elapsed. Sites that need faster or slower cleanup can set, for example:

// settings.php
$settings['package_manager_max_sandbox_age'] = 7; // days

item.description:

Summary

As part of converting the locale module to object-oriented code, six procedural helper functions in locale.module are now deprecated: locale_translation_use_remote_source(), locale_string_is_safe(), locale_translatable_language_list(), locale_js_translate(), locale_translation_language_table(), and locale_is_translatable(). Calling any of them now triggers a deprecation notice, and they will be removed in Drupal 13.0.0. Most gained a direct service or static-method replacement; two (locale_translation_use_remote_source() and locale_translation_language_table()) have no replacement because their logic was inlined into the code that used to call them. This only affects code that calls these functions directly (custom or contributed modules); regular site administrators are not affected.

Impact

Affects module maintainers.

  • Deprecation: Procedural functions locale_string_is_safe(), locale_translatable_language_list(), locale_is_translatable(), locale_js_translate(), locale_translation_language_table(), and locale_translation_use_remote_source() are deprecated in Drupal 11.5.0 and removed in 13.0.0.
  • New API: New Drupal\locale\LocaleLanguages service (getTranslatableLanguages(), isTranslatable()) and new Drupal\locale\LocaleXss class (stringIsSafe()) replace the deprecated locale functions.

Technical details

The deprecated function bodies now just call the new location and stay as thin wrappers that raise E_USER_DEPRECATED. locale_string_is_safe() moved verbatim to LocaleXss::stringIsSafe(). locale_translatable_language_list() and locale_is_translatable() moved to the new LocaleLanguages service (getTranslatableLanguages() and isTranslatable()). locale_js_translate() moved to the new LocaleJs::jsTranslate() service, but that class is marked @internal, so the deprecation message points to a service that isn't part of the committed public API. locale_translation_language_table()'s logic was moved into a new TranslationStatusForm::translationLanguageTable() method and wired up as the form's #after_build callback instead of the old procedural callback. locale_translation_use_remote_source() had no natural home, so every caller was changed to inline the underlying config check ($config->get('locale.settings')->get('translation.use_source') == LOCALE_TRANSLATION_USE_SOURCE_REMOTE_AND_LOCAL) directly.

Introducing LocaleLanguages (and, in one case, LocaleJs) as an injected dependency required adding a new constructor parameter to numerous locale classes that previously called the procedural functions: several services (LocaleFetch, LocaleProjectChecker, LocaleSource, LocaleConfigManager, LocaleFileManager), forms (ExportForm, ImportForm, TranslateFormBase, TranslationStatusForm), hook classes (LocaleHooks, LocaleFormHooks, LocaleThemeAlterHooks, a new LocaleThemeAlterHooks split out of the old LocaleFormHooks), LocaleRequirements, and the LocaleConfigSubscriber event subscriber. Several of these classes were also modernized to constructor property promotion in the same pass. LocaleThemeAlterHooks is a newly split-out class holding the hook_js_alter() and hook_library_info_alter() implementations that used to live in LocaleFormHooks, and it now injects LocaleJs via an #[AutowireServiceClosure] to avoid a hard circular/unnecessary dependency.

Upgrade

Replace direct calls to the deprecated functions:

// Before
locale_string_is_safe($string);
locale_translatable_language_list();
locale_is_translatable($langcode);
locale_js_translate($files, $language);

// After
\Drupal\locale\LocaleXss::stringIsSafe($string);
\Drupal::service(\Drupal\locale\LocaleLanguages::class)->getTranslatableLanguages();
\Drupal::service(\Drupal\locale\LocaleLanguages::class)->isTranslatable($langcode);
\Drupal::service(\Drupal\locale\LocaleJs::class)->jsTranslate($files, $language);

For locale_translation_use_remote_source() and locale_translation_language_table(), there is no replacement API; inline the equivalent logic:

// Before
locale_translation_use_remote_source();

// After
\Drupal::config('locale.settings')->get('translation.use_source') == LOCALE_TRANSLATION_USE_SOURCE_REMOTE_AND_LOCAL;

Summary

Drupal's test runner used to install a test's install profile first, then make a second call to install any extra modules listed in the test's static $modules property (and the default theme), each of which rebuilds the service container. This change lets those extra modules and the default theme be installed in the same pass as the profile's own modules and themes, cutting the number of container rebuilds during test setup and speeding up the test suite. There is no behavior change for site owners; it only affects how Drupal core and contrib tests execute. As part of the change, the method some test classes override to add modules, installModulesFromClassProperty(), is deprecated and will be removed in Drupal 13.

Impact

Affects module maintainers.

  • Deprecation: FunctionalTestSetupTrait::installModulesFromClassProperty() is deprecated in Drupal 12.0.0 and removed in 13.0.0; override getModulesFromClassProperty() instead to supply extra modules for a test.

Technical details

install_profile_modules() and install_profile_themes() in install.core.inc now read $install_state['extra_modules'] and $install_state['default_theme'] and merge them into the profile's own module and theme lists before making a single call to the module/theme installer, instead of installing the profile first and the extras separately. install_install_profile() also writes default_theme into system.theme config when present.

On the test side, FunctionalTestSetupTrait::installParameters() now populates those two install_state keys from a new getModulesFromClassProperty() method (which just returns the modules collected recursively from static::$modules) and from $this->defaultTheme. installDrupal() no longer calls installModulesFromClassProperty()/installDefaultThemeFromClassProperty() after the profile install step, because the extra modules and theme are now installed as part of the profile install itself. installModulesFromClassProperty() remains as a deprecated BC wrapper around getModulesFromClassProperty() for the few callers, such as PerformanceTestTrait, that still invoke it directly. WebDriverTestBase and PerformanceTestBase were switched from overriding installModulesFromClassProperty() to overriding getModulesFromClassProperty().

Because path_alias can now be installed in the same batch as another module that creates a path alias from its own hook_install(), PathAliasRepository::pathHasMatchingAlias() now catches DatabaseException and returns FALSE instead of fataling when its own table doesn't exist yet; a related edge case involving route-dependent modules is tracked separately in #3616642. Several test-only modules gained explicit dependencies in their .info.yml files (e.g. on layout_builder) because they could no longer rely on being installed after the module they depend on.

Upgrade

// Before:
protected function installModulesFromClassProperty(ContainerInterface $container): void {
  self::$modules = [
    'js_testing_ajax_request_test',
    'js_testing_log_test',
  ];
  parent::installModulesFromClassProperty($container);
}

// After:
protected function getModulesFromClassProperty(): array {
  $modules = parent::getModulesFromClassProperty();
  $modules = array_merge($modules, ['js_testing_ajax_request_test', 'js_testing_log_test']);
  return $modules;

Summary

Affects module maintainers.

The installer reads each profile's parsed info array into $install_state['profile_info'] (via install_profile_info()). install_install_profile() in install.core.inc now checks $install_state['profile_info']['opt_out_install'] before calling \Drupal::service('module_installer')->install() on the profile itself, skipping that call when the key is truthy. drupal_install_system() in install.inc was likewise updated so that the core.extension config's profile key is cleared (not just when there is no profile at all) whenever the profile has opted out, keeping the stored configuration consistent with the fact that the profile was never installed as a module.

This work builds on #3614153, which moved the System module install step earlier in the installer.

Add opt_out_install: true to an install profile's .info.yml if the profile has no hook_install() or other behavior that depends on being installed as a module:

item.title: #3577900: Require plugin managers that support annotation discovery to support attribute discovery
item.description:
• Project: Drupal Core
  • Type: Normal task
  • Version: main
  • Status: Fixed
  • Changes: 2 files, +2/−15 · php +2/−15
  • Diff: 460789d
  • Discussion: #3577900 · 5 contributors · 14 comments
  • Followers: 8

Summary

Drupal's plugin system has been moving from PHP annotations to PHP attributes for defining plugins. Since Drupal 11.2, plugin managers that only supported annotation-based discovery (and not the newer attribute-based discovery) triggered a silenced deprecation warning that was easy to miss. As of this change, any plugin manager, in core or in contributed and custom modules, that does not also provide an attribute class will now cause a fatal error when it is instantiated. This is intentional: since many contrib modules define plugin types that other contrib modules provide plugins for, forcing plugin-type-providing modules to add attribute support now (rather than waiting for Drupal 13) gives the wider ecosystem more time to update before the final removal of annotation-only discovery.

Impact

Affects module maintainers.

  • API change: Constructing DefaultPluginManager (or a subclass) with only $plugin_definition_annotation_name and no attribute class now throws an \InvalidArgumentException at construction time instead of triggering a silenced E_USER_DEPRECATED notice.

Technical details

The change is in DefaultPluginManager::__construct() in core/lib/Drupal/Core/Plugin/DefaultPluginManager.php. Previously, when a $plugin_definition_attribute_name was passed but did not implement AttributeInterface (i.e. only an annotation class was effectively usable), the constructor called @trigger_error(...) with E_USER_DEPRECATED, which is easy for sites and CI to ignore. Now it throws new \InvalidArgumentException(..., E_USER_WARNING) with a message pointing to the original deprecation change record (drupal.org node 3395582), so instantiating such a plugin manager fails outright rather than warning.

Accompanying core tests were updated: DefaultPluginManagerTest::testDefaultPluginManager() dropped its annotation-only assertions, and testDefaultPluginManagerAnnotationsOnly() now expects the thrown exception message instead of a deprecation message. This does not affect plugin managers that already provide both an attribute class and an annotation class for backward compatibility, which remains the supported pattern; only managers exposing annotation-only discovery are affected. This issue was tracked as a follow-up enforcement of the change documented in the existing change record https://www.drupal.org/node/3522776 (itself a "now you have to do it" successor to https://www.drupal.org/node/3395582 from 2023), so no new change record was created.

Upgrade

If you maintain a plugin manager that extends DefaultPluginManager (or implements similar annotation/attribute discovery) and it currently only supports annotation-based plugin discovery, you must add a PHP attribute class before upgrading to Drupal 12, or code that instantiates your plugin manager will throw:

InvalidArgumentException: Drupal\Your\Namespace\YourPluginManager only supports
annotation-based discovery, which is no longer supported as of Drupal 12.0.
Provide an Attribute class and an Annotation class for BC. See
https://www.drupal.org/node/3395582

To fix, define an Attribute class (implementing the plugin's attribute annotation pattern) and pass both the attribute and annotation class names to the parent constructor, e.g.:

parent::__construct(
  $subdir,
  $namespaces,
  $module_handler,
  $plugin_interface,
  MyPluginAttribute::class,
  MyPluginAnnotation::class
);

item.title: #3303751: Reduce the number of times UpdateRegistry scans for extensions
item.description:
• Project: Drupal Core
  • Type: Major task
  • Version: 11.x-dev
  • Status: Fixed
  • Changes: 5 files, +119/−34 · php +118/−33 · yml +1/−1
  • Diff: ee7c7d2
  • Discussion: #3303751 · 5 contributors · 40 comments
  • Followers: 9
  • AI disclosures: 0 of 5 contributors

Summary

Sites with a large number of enabled modules and themes were seeing significantly slower site installs, database updates, and test runs because UpdateRegistry (the service that tracks and runs hook_post_update_NAME() implementations) re-scanned the filesystem for every module, theme, and profile each time it needed to check for update files on a given extension. On a site or test suite with 150+ extensions, this added up to a large, repeated cost. The registry now scans the filesystem for extensions once and reuses the result, cutting a substantial amount of time off installs, updates, and functional test runs, especially on slower filesystems like Docker or WSL2.

Impact

Affects module maintainers.

  • Deprecation: Calling UpdateRegistry::__construct() without the new $memoryCache argument is deprecated in Drupal 11.5.0 and will be required in 12.0.0.

Technical details

The expensive work happened in UpdateRegistry::scanExtensionsAndLoadUpdateFiles(), which built a new ExtensionDiscovery and called scan('module'), scan('theme'), and scan('profile') on every invocation, even though the result rarely changes within a request. This logic was extracted into a new discoverExtensions() method that first checks an injected MemoryCacheInterface (cache.memory) for a cached copy under the update_registry.extensions cache ID, populating it and tagging it config:core.extension on a miss so it's invalidated automatically when the installed extension list changes (module/theme install or uninstall).

To get the memory cache into the class, UpdateRegistry::__construct() gained a new MemoryCacheInterface|string|null $memoryCache = NULL parameter inserted before the existing $updateType parameter. For backward compatibility, if a string is passed in that slot (the old calling convention where $updateType was the sixth argument) it's treated as $updateType and the memory cache falls back to \Drupal::service('cache.memory'), with a deprecation notice raised. The update.post_update_registry service definition in core.services.yml was updated to pass @cache.memory explicitly.

Upgrade

Update any code that instantiates UpdateRegistry directly (for example Drush's deploy hook command) to pass a MemoryCacheInterface service as the sixth constructor argument, before $updateType:

new UpdateRegistry(
  $root,
  $sitePath,
  $module_list,
  $keyValue,
  $theme_handler,
  \Drupal::service('cache.memory'),
  'post_update',
);

Calling the constructor without the $memoryCache argument still works in Drupal 11.5.x but triggers a deprecation notice and will be removed in Drupal 12.0.0.

Timeline

  • Opened: August 15, 2022
  • Committed: August 25, 2026 (4 years and 2 commits later)

An initial patch from the issue reporter (phma) sat for years before nicxvan and longwave reworked it: longwave proposed an alternative in MR!16818 that avoided threading a boolean flag through several methods and added test coverage proving discovery happens once and is then cached, which nicxvan preferred over the original patch. item.title: #2871354: Improve "allowed_html" to provide a better config diff
item.description:
• Project: Drupal Core
  • Type: Normal feature request
  • Version: 11.x-dev
  • Status: Fixed
  • Changes: 30 files, +233/−163 · php +216/−146 · yml +17/−17
  • Diff: 8f7a0cb
  • Discussion: #2871354 · 15 contributors · 126 comments
  • Followers: 23
  • AI disclosures: 0 of 15 contributors

Summary

Text formats that use the "Limit allowed HTML tags" filter store their list of permitted tags/attributes (allowed_html) as a single string. Because elements were historically just appended wherever the admin form or another module happened to place them, two functionally-identical configurations could produce very different-looking strings, making config exports hard to diff and hard to review in version control. Drupal now sorts that list alphabetically whenever it is saved, so equivalent configurations always serialize to the same string and future changes show up as small, readable diffs instead of noise. A one-time update also re-sorts allowed_html on any existing filter format that has Filter HTML enabled, and CKEditor 5's internal list of allowed elements is sorted the same way for consistency.

Impact

Affects site owners.

  • Config change: The allowed_html setting stored by the Filter HTML (filter_html) plugin is now kept alphabetically sorted; existing filter formats are resorted by a new filter_post_update_sort_allowed_html() update, producing a one-time config diff.

Technical details

The fix lands the simple approach originally proposed in this issue rather than the redesigned, structured schema (nested sequences keyed by element/attribute) that was prototyped and reviewed at length over several years: that redesign hit an unresolved backwards-compatibility problem, since Drupal's config schema has no version tracking, so changing allowed_html from a string to a sequence risked breaking config import from sites still exporting the old string format, a concern raised in the thread by Gábor Hojtsy and effulgentsia.

Instead, FilterHtml::setConfiguration() now runs the incoming allowed_html string through a new public static method, FilterHtml::sortAllowedHtmlTags(), which extracts each <tag attrs> token with a regex and sorts them with sort($tags, SORT_STRING) before re-imploding them. The schema and stored representation remain an unstructured string, so no BC-breaking schema change was needed. A new filter_post_update_sort_allowed_html() (filter.post_update.php) uses ConfigEntityUpdater to resave every filter_format config entity that has an enabled filter_html filter, so the sort applies retroactively without requiring an admin to resave the format manually. Separately, HTMLRestrictions::toCKEditor5ElementsArray() now calls sort($readable) on its own generated element list for the same consistency reason, which is why CKEditor 5 test expectations for allowed-tag strings changed throughout the patch.

Summary

The Status Report page (admin/reports/status) now lists the actual database connection details, host, database name, and table prefix, for every configured database connection, not just the default one. Previously the status page gave no indication of which database(s) a site was actually connected to, which made it easy to mix up databases when cloning or migrating sites for testing. Summary

For new sites installed with the Standard profile, Drupal no longer installs or enables the Olivero theme. Claro becomes both the admin theme and the default front end theme. The site's front page is now a new /admin/welcome page that explains the difference between Drupal Core and Drupal CMS and lists first steps (build a content model, pick a theme, extend Drupal), plus how to change the front page or remove the welcome page by uninstalling the Standard profile. Because that page requires an administration permission, anonymous visitors to the homepage now see a login block instead. None of this affects existing sites: the theme switch and welcome page only apply to fresh Standard profile installs, upgrading a site changes nothing. Installs done via the standard recipe (the CLI/recipe based path) also skip the welcome page and no longer pull in a separate recipe that installed Olivero as the front end theme, since Claro is now set directly.

Impact

Affects site owners.

  • Config change: Fresh Standard profile installs now set claro as both the admin and default (front end) theme instead of olivero, and set /admin/welcome as the site's front page instead of /user/login.

In core/profiles/standard, standard.info.yml no longer lists olivero under themes, and the profile's shipped system.theme config sets default: claro (was olivero). system.site.yml's page.front is now /admin/welcome instead of /user/login.
